confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail: Keshavrao's line "Look. The ring." has its tail on Nagoji.
confirmed.evidence: The balloon sits at the far left and its tail ends at Nagoji's ear and cheek (curly hair, gold stud, ochre tunic). Keshavrao is on the right with his mouth open, looking up at the chain. The script (4.5) gives the line to Keshavrao.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at 300 DPI (crop of page 4, panel 5). The "Look. The ring." balloon sits at the far left of the panel and its tail ends right at the ear of the left-hand figure. That figure is Nagoji: long curly hair, heavy moustache, gold ear stud, ochre torn tunic, mouth closed. Keshavrao is on the far right (short ragged hair, faint moustache, iron collar). His mouth is open and he is looking up at the chain, but no tail reaches him. Script 4.5 gives the line to KESHAVRAO. The staging note says he "shouts into the ear of Nagoji", but comic convention points a tail at the speaker, never at the listener's ear, so readers will take the line as Nagoji's. Nothing in the bible or script allows this, and at print size the balloon is large and plainly attached to Nagoji. A side effect: with the balloon at far left, it is read before the prisoner's "We will drown down here", which reverses the script's order. The prisoner's tail is correct (it points at the open-mouthed middle prisoner). This is a localized lettering fix: move the balloon to the right and aim its tail at Keshavrao's mouth, placed after the prisoner's balloon. It does not need a redraw, so it is major rather than a blocker.

confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail: Nagoji's count "One, two..." has its tail on Keshavrao.
confirmed.evidence: The right-hand balloon's tail ends beside Keshavrao's head (short ragged hair, grey-brown tunic). In the script both 5.4 lines belong to Nagoji. The left balloon, "On three...", correctly points at Nagoji.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the problem. The script gives both 5.4 lines to Nagoji: "On three. Pull as if..." and then "One, two...". On the page, the right-hand "One, two..." balloon sits right next to Keshavrao. A zoomed crop of that area (about x 1000-1500, y 1480-1800 on the full-size image) shows its tail ending just above the top-left of his hair, almost touching it. Nagoji's head is roughly 300+ px to the left at full resolution. The tail does point left, so a line drawn on from the tip would pass near Nagoji. But readers go by where the tip ends, and it ends on Keshavrao. At print size a reader will take Keshavrao as the one counting. Nothing in the script or cast overrides allows this. The left balloon ("On three...") correctly points at Nagoji. The mistake is small and confined to one balloon: the tail needs to be redirected to Nagoji, or the two lines joined into one balloon linked to him. The art itself can stay. Because this is a wrong speaker tail that takes the leader's count away from him, it is major, not a blocker.

confirmed.description: The two speaker tails are swapped. "Others." points at Nagoji and "Quickly." points at Keshavrao, the reverse of the script.
confirmed.evidence: The top-left balloon "Others." has its tail on the ochre-tunic Nagoji. The top-right balloon "Quickly." has its tail on Keshavrao. In the script (6.1), KESHAVRAO says "Others." and NAGOJI says "Quickly."

verdict.reason: I zoomed in on page 6, panel 1 and the reviewer is right. The figure on the left has long curly hair, a moustache, an earring, an ochre tunic and bandaged hands. That matches Nagoji as he appears in panel 6.2 on the same page. The figure on the right has short hair and a grey-brown tunic, which is Keshavrao. The tail of the top-left balloon ("Others.") ends at the left figure's head, so it points at Nagoji. The tail of the top-right balloon ("Quickly.") runs leftward and ends at the right figure's head, so it points at Keshavrao. Script 6.1 gives the lines the other way round: KESHAVRAO says "Others." and NAGOJI says "Quickly." That makes Nagoji the one who proposes freeing the other prisoners, which is Keshavrao's beat. The lines are still read in the right order, so this is a wrong speaker tail on one panel, which is major rather than blocker. There is a second, smaller mismatch: the script asks for both balloons at the left, but they sit at opposite corners. Fix: swap the two tails, or swap the two texts.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's reply "If we stay, we may drown before they can load." is linked by a connector to Keshavrao's balloon, so it reads as Keshavrao's line.
confirmed.evidence: The lower balloon has no tail of its own. A connector joins it to the "If we take it, they will shoot us." balloon, and that balloon's tail points at Keshavrao on the right. The script gives the reply to NAGOJI.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. On page 6, panel 2, the balloon "If we stay, we may drown before they can load." has a wedge tail, but the tail never reaches a speaker. It runs up-left and its tip stops inside the "If we take it, they will shoot us." balloon, on the "o" of "shoot". Keshavrao's balloon is drawn over the tail, but the tail's outline still shows inside its white area. In comics, a tail that ends inside another balloon reads as a connector, which means the same speaker. That balloon's own tail points right at Keshavrao, so the rebuttal reads as Keshavrao talking to himself. The lower balloon also sits mostly over Keshavrao's torso, which makes it worse. The script gives this line to NAGOJI (6.2). The tail's angle suggests it was meant to point at Nagoji's face on the left, but it stops short and lands in the wrong balloon. This is clearly visible at print size, since both tail edges are bold black lines. The rubric lists "wrong speaker tail" as major. The fix is local: re-letter the tail so it runs past the upper balloon to Nagoji on the left. I read the reviewer's "no tail of its own" as meaning the tail works as a connector, not that it is literally missing.

confirmed.description: Nagoji is off the captivity sheet here. His hands and wrists are bare under the manacles, and his left forearm, stretched to the rail, has no tunic flap over it.
confirmed.evidence: In a zoomed crop both manacles close on bare skin, with no linen wrapping. His torso faces camera and his left arm (viewer's right) reaches bare to the rail. The bandages are back in the 9.1 inset and are torn away in 9.5, so this panel breaks that setup. The bible's chapter 3 row requires bandaged hands and wrists and a covered left arm.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 8, panel 1 (the first third of the page, Nagoji at the starboard rail on the right). In a zoomed crop both manacles close directly on bare brown skin. There is no linen at either wrist, and his bare fingers are on the rope and the rail. Continuity is broken on the same page: in 8.3 his wrist is clearly wrapped in white linen under the manacle, and page 9 (the 9.1 inset, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4) shows the bandages on both hands. That setup matters, because 9.5 and 10.1 pay it off with the bandages stripped. Several sources require the bandages: the CONTINUITY.md chapter 3 row ("bandaged hands and wrists"), the script's 1.1 and closing Continuity note ("Nagoji wears the captivity sheet throughout ... bandaged hands and wrists"), and the V13 captivity sheet (thick wrist wraps). The left arm is a weaker point. It is stretched bare to the rail with no tunic flap, which the script's 1.1 rule forbids ("A ragged flap of the torn tunic hangs over his left forearm ... keep that forearm covered or turned from camera in every panel"). But we see the outer or upper side of the forearm, the inner side faces down, and no brand mark is visible. So the brand is not revealed, and on that part alone this is at most a technicality. The missing bandages are easy to see at print size: the panel takes a third of the page and Nagoji is large in the frame, so the jump from bare wrists in 8.1 to wrapped wrists in 8.3 is noticeable. This is a localized costume and continuity error, not an identity failure, so major rather than blocker. Fix: redraw 8.1 with linen wraps on both hands and wrists under the manacles, and ideally add the tunic flap over the left forearm.

confirmed.description: Missing beat: Nagoji never grabs Keshavrao. The panel's only action (Keshavrao loses his grip, Nagoji clamps a bandaged hand on his forearm, and the wrist chain clangs on Keshavrao's cuffs) is not drawn.
confirmed.evidence: The two men lean forward several feet apart, with a pillar between them. Their hands are cropped off at the bottom edge. There is no contact, no grip and no wrist chain striking anything. The panel is silent, so nothing else carries the beat.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 3, panel 3. The script (3.3) calls for the ship to roll, Keshavrao to lose his grip, and Nagoji to clamp his bandaged hand onto Keshavrao's forearm, with Nagoji's wrist chain clanging on Keshavrao's cuffs. The panel is silent, so the art has to carry all of this. I cropped and zoomed the panel. Nagoji is at the left and Keshavrao at the right-centre, leaning forward and roughly 400px apart at page scale. A rope-wrapped pillar stands between them. Both men's forearms and hands run off the bottom panel border. The only other visible hand is Keshavrao's right hand, resting on a barrel at the far right edge. They never touch and nobody grips anyone. No bandaged hand is visible, and no manacle chain between the wrists is drawn. The only chains visible are the collar chains. Nothing shows Keshavrao losing his grip or falling. The script does not allow for this, and the effect is not too slight to see: at print size the panel reads as two men crouching apart. It drops the rescue that sets up the 3.4 two-shot and Nagoji taking command. Under the rubric, a missing beat is a blocker.

confirmed.description: Missing beat: Keshavrao does not have the rope. The script needs him half out of the hatch, fumbling the rope end round his chest while his wrist chain catches on it. That sets up 9.4 ('I thought he had managed it') and the break in 9.5.
confirmed.evidence: Keshavrao looks down with empty hands. The rope runs from Nagoji's bandaged hands (left edge) out through the bottom of the frame and never reaches him. No hatch is visible and there is no rope near his chest.

verdict.reason: The problem is real, but it is a crop problem rather than a missing beat. I zoomed into panel 9.3 (page-09.png, roughly y 1410 to 1690 at full resolution). The rope runs from Nagoji's bandaged hands on the left and leaves the bottom border at about x 650, before it gets to Keshavrao. Keshavrao is cut off at mid-chest: his right arm goes down past the frame and only a glint of his wrist cuff shows at the bottom border. No rope is visible anywhere near his chest, and there is no hatch. The script's action for this panel (rope end in his manacled hands, fumbling it round his chest, the short wrist chain catching) is not shown, although the wave rearing behind him on the right is there. The reviewer's evidence goes too far when it says his hands are empty. His hands are simply outside the frame. Because the rope heads toward his lower body and he is looking down at it, a reader can still guess he is taking hold of it, so 9.4 ("I thought he had managed it") and the break in 9.5 still make sense in a weaker form. That makes this the "awkward crop hiding the action" case, which is major, not a blocker. Fix: redraw or reframe 9.3 so the rope reaches his hands at his chest and the chain snag is visible inside the strip.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's hands and wrists are unbandaged, and his wrist chain is missing. Chapter 3 has him bandaged throughout, with the manacles joined by a short chain.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed, both manacles sit on bare skin with no bandage on either hand. The right manacle (on the rope coil) has a short broken chain end, and the left one (on the rail) has none. No chain links the two, even though the hands are about a torso-width apart. His left forearm reaching to the rail is bare, with no tunic flap. Every other deck panel (8.3, 9.x, 10.x) shows bandages.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 8, panel 1. Zoomed crops of Nagoji (original pixels about x1380-1690, y570-880) show both hands and wrists as bare, wet skin, with no linen anywhere. His right wrist, on the rope coil, has a doubled iron cuff and a short broken chain end hanging from it. His left wrist, on the rail, has a cuff with a small ring and no chain. Nothing joins the two cuffs, and his hands are almost a full arm span apart, which a chain about a forearm long could not allow.

This goes against the bible's chapter 3 row ("bandaged hands and wrists ... wrist manacles joined by a short chain about a forearm long") and the script. Script 8.1 says "He wears his empty iron collar, wrist chain and hobble chain", and the continuity note has him in "bandaged hands and wrists" throughout, with every iron kept on into the sea.

It is not too slight to matter. This is the page's big establishing panel, and Nagoji is its largest figure with his hands in plain view. The very next panels show thick bandages and a linked wrist chain: 8.3 at the rail, then 9.1 inset, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4 and 9.5. The bandages also set up the 9.5 beat, where the rope strips them.

One part of the claim is weaker. The bare left forearm with no tunic flap is not a brand exposure: his hand grips the rail palm-down, so the inner forearm faces away from camera, which the bible allows ("covered or turned from camera"), and no brand is drawn. The main error is the missing bandages and the unjoined manacles. It is a localized costume and continuity fault in one panel, not an identity or beat failure, so it is major rather than a blocker.

confirmed.description: The hatch ladder has turned into a broad plank staircase, and the hobble chain is missing: Nagoji's ankles are a full stride apart. This breaks with 6.4 and 7.2, where he is on a narrow rung ladder, and with the captions 'The ladder felt narrower…' and 'The ladder was clear.' 7.3 also shows wide stairs at the foot.
confirmed.evidence: 7.1 shows a wide staircase with side stringers, the guard standing on it and Nagoji lunging beside it. His left ankle cuff trails a loose broken chain end, and his right foot is two steps up with no chain between the ankles. In 7.2 the same ladder is narrow, with square rungs. 7.3's bottom edge shows a wide stair of planks.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 7, panel 1. At zoom, the hatch ladder is drawn as a broad plank staircase: deep flat treads set between heavy side stringers, several times wider than the square-rung ladder in 6.4 and 7.2. Nagoji is not on the ladder at all. He is lunging from the water beside its foot, right foot on a tread and left foot in the water, a full stride apart. There is no hobble chain between his ankles, and the left ankle cuff trails a two-link stub that reads as a broken chain. The script requires ankle cuffs on a short hobble chain for the whole chapter: 6.4 says 'the hobble chain cuts every step short', and the notes say 'every iron stays on into the sea'. So this panel wrongly suggests his ankles are free. It also clashes with the 6.4 caption ('The ladder felt narrower than any siege stair I had ever mounted') and with 7.2, where the ladder is narrow and rung-built and his ankles are chained close together. The bottom edge of 7.3 also shows wide plank treads, but that is a smaller inconsistency; seen from above, a companion ladder with flat treads is defensible. The problem is confined to one panel and clearly visible at print size. It is a costume and prop continuity error, not wrong identity or a missing beat, so major rather than blocker.

confirmed.description: There are several problems with the set, the prop and the render. The ladder is drawn as a wide staircase with handrails, unlike the rung ladder in 1.4 and 1.5. A solid black band fills the top of the panel. The caption box hides most of the musket, which this panel exists to plant.
confirmed.evidence: There is an empty black strip roughly 90 px deep at 1838 px width across the whole top of the 2.4 frame. At right, a broad plank staircase rises to grey light. Only the musket's lock shows, under the caption 'Too far to reach…'. In 2.3 the same staircase stands between Nagoji and Keshavrao, who now sit yards apart, although in 2.1 they sit shoulder to shoulder in one pen.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 2, panel 4. (1) A solid black strip runs across the full width of the 2.4 frame, from about y=2258 to y=2348 in the 1838 px render. That is roughly 90 px of pure black, measured at a mean row value of 0.0. At 300 DPI it is about 0.3 in deep and takes up nearly a third of a panel only about 300 px tall. This is an obvious layout or render defect at print size. (2) The caption 'Too far to reach. Too close to ignore.' sits in the upper-left of the remaining art. What is left of the musket is squeezed into the bottom strip and cut off by the frame edge: the butt, part of the stock and the flintlock show, but the barrel and the thin current curling round the stock (script 2.4) do not. The prop this panel exists to plant for page 6 therefore reads only partially. (3) At right, the 'ladder' is a broad plank staircase with side rails rising to grey sky. It does not match the narrow rung ladder under the hatch in 1.4 and 1.5. The same lit staircase stands between Nagoji and Keshavrao in 2.3, who sit well apart there although they share one chain and pen in 2.1. Each problem is localized to this frame (plus a background inconsistency in 2.3) and does not involve a wrong identity or missing lettering, so this is major rather than blocker. The fix is to regenerate or recrop 2.4 without the black band, with the musket and the current fully in frame under the caption, and a rung ladder consistent with 1.4 and 1.5.

confirmed.description: The musket plant is too weak. The script says to plant it hard, with the musket in the foreground and every head turned to it. Here it is a sliver at the frame edge and nobody looks at it.
confirmed.evidence: Only the lock and a few inches of stock show at the bottom right, cut off by the frame. Nagoji and Keshavrao look down at their laps, and the prisoners in the background look toward the camera.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 2, panel 1. Script 2.1 asks for the musket large in the foreground with every chained head turned to it, and the page note says to "plant it hard" because it pays off on page 6. In the art, the musket is only a flintlock and a few inches of barrel or stock. It sits in the bottom-right corner (about x 1260-1690, y 1000-1060 of the 1838x2775 render), cut off by the bottom frame line and half lost in shadow under the post. At print size it is about 0.9 x 0.2 inches, and you have to hunt for it. Nobody reacts to it. Nagoji and Keshavrao have their heads bowed with eyes lowered toward their manacled hands and laps. The two background prisoners who can be read clearly (the curly-haired man and the bald man) look out toward the viewer on the left, not down and right at the gun. That contradicts both captions ("They draw every eye in a space" and "the shape of power"), so the words describe something the picture does not show. It is not a blocker, because the beat is not missing from the page: panel 2.4 shows the musket (lock and stock visible under the caption), and Nagoji's line in 2.3 names it. The plant still exists but is weakened. This is a localized staging and crop error in one panel, so major is the right severity. Fix: redraw 2.1 with the musket in the foreground and the heads (Keshavrao's especially) turned toward it.

confirmed.description: Chain and ring continuity is broken, against the rule that no chain hangs vertically above a head. The ring hangs on a vertical chain from the beam directly above the men's heads, not on its last bolt at the far end of the chain they haul. Both collars are already empty, although the pen chain is only stripped out of them in 5.5. The hauled chain is also much heavier, near anchor-chain gauge, than the pen chain in 5.2.
confirmed.evidence: At top centre, a ring hangs from a staple, with a chain dropping straight down between Nagoji's and Keshavrao's heads. Both collar side rings are empty. In 5.1 the ring is bolted flat to the beam with the chain leaving it at a slant.

verdict.reason: Confirmed after zooming in on page 5, panel 4. At top centre an undamaged ring hangs from a staple in the beam, and a chain drops straight down from it into the gap between Nagoji's and Keshavrao's heads. It ends behind Nagoji's shoulder. Script 1.1 and the chapter notes rule this out ("No chain ever hangs vertical above a head"). Beat 5.4 also asks for the ring to hang on its last bolt at the far end of the hauled chain. Instead, the ring is intact with no splintering, even though 5.2 showed it torn half out and hanging from one bolt. It is also not connected to the chain the men are pulling, which runs from their fists toward the camera and out of frame. That breaks the cause and effect of the escape: their pull should be what rips out the last bolt in 5.5. Both collar side rings are clearly empty, even though 5.3 shows the pen chain still through Nagoji's collar ring, and in the script the chain only runs out of the collars in 5.5. The hauled chain is also much heavier than the pen chain in 5.2: at fist level each link is about as wide as a fist, far thicker than the thin pen chain, so foreground perspective does not explain it. All of this is prominent and readable at print size. It is limited to one panel, with no identity or lettering fault, so it is major rather than a blocker.

confirmed.description: The tail is on the wrong speaker. 'One, two...' is Nagoji's line, but its tail points to Keshavrao.
confirmed.evidence: The right-hand balloon's tail ends just above Keshavrao's head. Both lines in the panel belong to Nagoji.

verdict.reason: I could not refute this one. Script 5.4 gives both lines to Nagoji ("On three..." and "One, two..."). In the zoomed crop, the left balloon's tail correctly points at Nagoji, who is on the left, near (720,1580). The right balloon "One, two..." has a short tail pointing left, and its tip ends at about (1142,1578) at full resolution. That is about 20 to 40 px above and slightly left of Keshavrao's hair, whose crown is near (1170,1595). It is about 400 px, roughly 1.3 in at print size, from Nagoji's face. Readers attribute a balloon to the head nearest its tail tip, so they will read "One, two..." as Keshavrao's count. Nothing in the script or the bible allows that. The tail's horizontal line does roughly aim toward Nagoji's head. But it stops over Keshavrao, and at print size it clearly lands on the wrong character. The damage stays inside this one panel, since Keshavrao counting is plausible and the story beat still reads. That fits the rubric's "wrong speaker tail" = major, not blocker. Fix: extend the tail toward Nagoji, or join the two balloons with a connector.

confirmed.description: The tail is on the wrong speaker. 'Look. The ring.' is Keshavrao's line, but the tail goes into Nagoji's head.
confirmed.evidence: The left balloon's tail ends at Nagoji's ear, while Keshavrao is at the right with his mouth open. The PRISONER balloon's tail is correct.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on a zoomed crop of page 4, panel 5 (page-04.png, about x140-1700, y2070-2550 at full resolution). The tail of the "Look. The ring." balloon at upper left ends right at the left figure's ear. That figure is Nagoji: long curly hair, heavy moustache, gold earring and ochre tunic, the same as in 4.1, and his mouth is shut. Keshavrao is the figure on the right: short ragged hair, faint moustache and grey-brown tunic, the same as in 4.2, and his mouth is open. Script 4.5 gives "Look. The ring." to Keshavrao and places him on the right and Nagoji on the left, so a reader will take the line as Nagoji's. The script's wording that Keshavrao "shouts into the ear of Nagoji" describes the staging only. By normal lettering practice the tail points at the speaker, so it does not excuse the tail. The PRISONER tail correctly lands on the open-mouthed bearded man in the middle. The error is easy to see at print size, but the balloon text is right and the fix is local: move the tail to Keshavrao on the right, or move the balloon to his side. The rubric lists a wrong speaker tail as major, so I rate it major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: The speaker tails are swapped. 'Others.' (Keshavrao) points to Nagoji, and 'Quickly.' (Nagoji) points to Keshavrao.
confirmed.evidence: The upper-left 'Others.' balloon's tail runs to Nagoji's head, and the upper-right 'Quickly.' balloon's tail runs to Keshavrao.

verdict.reason: I confirmed it on a zoomed crop of page 6, panel 1. The script gives "KESHAVRAO: Others." and then "NAGOJI: Quickly." The two men are easy to tell apart. The left figure is Nagoji: long curly hair, gold ear stud, ochre tunic, bandaged wrist. He matches the left figure in 6.2, which the script names as Nagoji. The right figure is Keshavrao: short hacked black hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic and no ear stud, which fits his CONTINUITY.md line. The upper-left "Others." balloon's tail ends at the left man's head, so Keshavrao's line comes from Nagoji. The upper-right "Quickly." balloon's tail ends at the right man's head, so Nagoji's line comes from Keshavrao. The error is plain at print size, and neither the script nor the bible allows it. Both lines are attributed to the wrong man. Under the brief's rubric a wrong speaker tail is major. It is a lettering fix and the art does not need redrawing. The script also asks for both balloons at the left, at the start of the move, which this layout ignores. The fix is to point "Others." at Keshavrao and "Quickly." at Nagoji and keep "Others." first in reading order. Simply swapping the two texts would put the lines in the wrong order.

confirmed.description: The third balloon reads as Keshavrao's. 'If we stay, we may drown before they can load.' is Nagoji's line, but its tail joins Keshavrao's balloon, and the tail tip also runs over the word 'shoot'.
confirmed.evidence: The tail of the lower balloon climbs into the middle 'If we take it, they will shoot us.' balloon, whose own tail points to Keshavrao. The tail stroke crosses the letters of 'shoot'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed from zoomed crops of page 6, panel 2. The script gives "If we stay, we may drown before they can load." to Nagoji, who stands on the left. The lower balloon's tail does not point at him. It climbs up and to the left into the middle balloon ("If we take it, they will shoot us."), and that middle balloon's own tail points right to Keshavrao. The stroke ends inside the text and runs over the "o" of "shoot". A tail joined to another balloon reads as that speaker continuing, so both lines land on Keshavrao and Nagoji's rebuttal is lost. The lettering over "shoot" is also untidy, although the word still reads. Nothing in the script or continuity bible allows this. The rubric counts a wrong speaker tail as major, not blocker, because the words are right and the fix is small: redraw one tail so it points down and left to Nagoji and stays off the lettering.

confirmed.description: The balloons read in the wrong order. 'Then we die here in the dark.' should come first, but it sits below and after 'You have seen the dungeon… Tell me which death you prefer.'
confirmed.evidence: The 'You have seen the dungeon' balloon starts around y≈570 (in the 1325 px view), and 'Then we die here in the dark.' sits in the bottom-left corner around y≈800, so a reader takes the second line first.

verdict.reason: Confirmed from a zoomed crop of page 4, panel 1. The "You have seen the dungeon... Tell me which death you prefer." balloon is on the right, and its top edge is at about y=790 of the full 1838x2775 render. The "Then we die here in the dark." balloon sits in the bottom-left corner under Keshavrao's back, with its top at about y=1055. The two balloons overlap vertically only at their edges, and their text starts about an inch apart at print size. Readers take the higher balloon first, so the order comes out reversed. The script (4.1) wants "Then we die here in the dark." first, as Nagoji's direct answer to Keshavrao's closing line on page 3 ("And if there is no such thing?"). The dungeon line should follow and set up Keshavrao's reply in 4.2 ("With you, I prefer the one that involves a chance."). With the order flipped, the "Then" line reads as a leftover after "Tell me which death you prefer." That breaks the question-and-answer rhythm of the exchange. The "Then" balloon's tail also ends right next to Keshavrao's shoulder, so the line could be misread as his. The script has no staging note that allows this order. The fix is lettering only, not a redraw: move "Then we die here in the dark." to the top left of the panel, above the dungeon balloon, or lower the dungeon balloon. That makes it a localized major problem, not a blocker.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's tunic has sleeves. The bible and captivity sheet specify a torn ochre sleeveless tunic, as drawn in 1.1 directly above.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed, both of Nagoji's arms are covered by long, ragged ochre sleeves down to the wrist bandages. In 1.1 his shoulders and arms are bare. The same sleeves recur in 9.3 (the ochre sleeve down to the manacle at the left edge).

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In the zoomed crop of page 1, panel 2, Nagoji wears a long-sleeved ochre tunic, and ragged sleeves cover both arms down to the wrist bandages and manacles. Directly above, in 1.1, the same tunic is sleeveless and his shoulders and upper arms are bare. The bible's chapter 3 row (CONTINUITY.md line 29) and the script (1.1 and the continuity note) both specify a "torn ochre sleeveless tunic". The script does allow one exception, a ragged flap of tunic draped over his LEFT forearm to hide the brand. minors.evidence: Page 2, panel 2: the left balloon's tail ends at about display x 540, and the guard's silhouette is at x about 640-780.

minors.description: The off-panel balloon for Nagoji is cut flat by the top and left frame lines. Its tail points down into the beam, so the ring seems to be the speaker; an off-panel tail should run to the frame edge.
minors.evidence: Page 5, panel 1: the 'When it goes, we move.' balloon has a straight top and left edge on the border, and its tail ends on the beam at around display 330,450.

minors.description: The caption box covers Nagoji's lower leg, the hobble chain and the lower rungs. The script makes the hobble chain cutting every step short part of this shot.
minors.evidence: Page 6, panel 4: 'The ladder felt narrower than any siege stair I had ever mounted.' sits at display x 425-658, y 1700-1822, over the ladder foot and ankle irons.

minors.description: This panel has a doubled frame: an inner black border sits about 10 px inside the outer border, with a cream band between them. No other panel does this, and it looks like a frame painted into the art.
minors.evidence: Page 7, panel 4: at a zoom on the top-left corner, the outer rule and an inner rule are separated by a cream margin along the left and top edges.

minors.description: The balloon is far too big for one word. It is flattened against the top frame line, runs to the right border and covers the storm sky.
minors.evidence: Page 8, panel 2: the 'Sahib!' balloon spans about display x 805-1215, y 712-900.

minors.description: The tail of Nagoji's shout points at the rope loop in the middle of the deck, not at Nagoji. The balloon is also cut flat by the bottom frame line.
minors.evidence: Page 9, panel 2: the tail of 'Tie it! Around your chest! Quick!' ends at the rope coil at around display 670,905. Nagoji's head is at around 470,670.

minors.description: The script puts the narration caption in the upper-left inset of Nagoji's hand. It is placed top right beside Keshavrao's face instead, which weakens the link between the caption and the inset.
minors.evidence: Page 9, panel 1: 'For a moment I was nowhere...' sits at display x 748-1155, y 260-355, and the inset is at x 108-443.

minors.description: The caption boxes are oversized, with large empty padding. The lower-right box covers the ship's rail falling away behind him.
minors.evidence: Page 10, panel 4: the 'To whatever gods listen to men who jump into storms.' box spans about display x 810-1215, y 1398-1565 for two lines, over the hull and rail at the right.

minors.description: The script asks for a close two-shot with Keshavrao's eyes on the musket, Nagoji's on the hatch, and seawater starting to thread past their feet. The render is a wide shot with the men far apart and Keshavrao looking down at his hands. No water crosses the boards near their feet, and a lit staircase fills the background.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, third panel (y~1735-2250): the two figures sit about 600 px apart; Keshavrao's gaze is down; the floor around their feet is dry.

minors.description: The script has both forearms hooked over the timber with the manacled wrists together over the wood. Nagoji instead has his arms apart: one hand grips a post, and the other raised arm is wrapped in the ochre flap with no manacle visible. A pen chain rises diagonally from behind his neck to the overhead beam. The '(in Marathi)' tag the adaptation notes call for is not lettered.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, second strip (y~825-1155): Nagoji's arms are spread at x~600 and x~1000-1250; a chain climbs from behind his collar at ~x 1000, y 1000 up to the top frame edge. The balloons carry plain English with no language tag.

minors.description: The silent release loses its action. The script has the freed chain end whip out through the collar side rings and slide into the water, with the splash as the line. The render shows only the two men apart looking up. No chain or splash is visible, and the waist-deep water from 5.4 is gone.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, bottom strip (y~2255-2545): both men look up, collars empty; there is no chain in motion and no water surface in frame.

minors.description: The page layout has large dead gutters. Blank cream bands, each about the height of a panel strip, sit between 5.3 and 5.4 and between 5.4 and 5.5, and 5.2 sits lower than 5.1.
minors.evidence: page-05.png: empty cream space at y~1240-1440 and y~2060-2255; the top edge of the 5.2 frame is at y~385 against y~360 for 5.1.

minors.description: The script asks for a high angle looking down the hatch shaft at Keshavrao climbing: thin manacled hands on the top of the ladder, bare hobbled ankles on a rung below, lit by lightning (review note: '8.2 shows the wrist and ankle irons'). The render is a head-and-shoulders close-up. No hands, manacles, ladder or ankle irons are visible, so it reads as him leaning over a crate, not climbing out of the hold.
minors.evidence: page-08.png, second strip (y~980-1450): only the head, collar and shoulders are in frame; there are no rungs or hands.

minors.description: Nagoji's POV should look straight up the ladder at a guard coming down. The render frames the guard at eye level in an upright, door-like opening, so it reads as a doorway rather than an overhead hatch. That clashes with 7.1, where the guard is above Nagoji.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, bottom-right panel: a vertical rectangular opening with a door ring on the right jamb; the guard's silhouette stands in it at the same height as the camera.

minors.description: The spar riding the foam below the rail is hidden behind the 'Forgive me.' balloon, and the balloon's tail points at the frayed rope end rather than Nagoji's mouth.
minors.evidence: page-10.png, panel 3: the splintered spar end is visible only as a sliver at ~x 1450-1530, y 1480 behind the balloon; the tail tip is at ~x 930, y 1480 by the rope end, well below Nagoji's face (~x 780, y 1330).

minors.description: The guard wears a round wide-brimmed hat, not the steel morion with upturned brim and crest that the script specifies and that 2.2, 6.5 and 7.1 show. The oversized second balloon also covers most of the ladder and the rain sheet.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, panel 4: the guard's hat at ~x 700-850, y 1680-1800 is a rounded brim with no crest; the balloon spans x~760-1690, y~1830-2140.

minors.description: The script frames this from below, looking up past Nagoji as he sinks, with his manacled hands and the knotted rope at the bottom edge. The render shows him from the front at the surface line, face serenely upturned. His hands and wrist irons are out of frame, so 'every iron stays on into the sea' is not shown.
minors.evidence: page-10.png, bottom strip (y~2200-2545): Nagoji's head is at the waterline; the frame cuts off at mid-chest with the rope knot visible but no hands or manacles.

minors.description: The caption 'For a moment I was nowhere...' should sit inside the inset of Nagoji's fingers in the rope coil. It is placed in the main image over Keshavrao instead.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, panel 1: the inset is at upper-left (x~150-615, y~360-615); the caption box is at upper-right (x~1035-1605, y~360-490).

minors.description: The script asks for jagged, overlapping off-panel balloons for the shouting sailors above. The render uses standard smooth ovals, and the first balloon has no tail at all.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, panel 3: the smooth rounded balloons 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' (no tail) and 'Tie that down!...' are separate and do not overlap.
